subject: Mythology
title: The Tortoise Trickster: Nigerian Folktales
description: A quick win: understand The Tortoise Trickster: Nigerian Folktales.

hook.text: In Igbo and Yoruba tales, the tortoise is the greediest, cleverest, and most entertaining trickster in all of Africa.

buildup.text: He tricks birds into lending him feathers so he can fly to a feast in the sky meant only for birds.

discovery.text: At the feast, he declares his name is 'All of You,' so when food is served 'for all of you,' he eats everything.

twist.text: The furious birds take back their feathers mid-flight. The tortoise falls and cracks his shell on the ground below.

climax.text: That is why the tortoise shell has cracks. Every African child who hears this story remembers not to be greedy.

punchline.text: The tortoise's cracked shell is a permanent lesson about what greed costs.

quiz.question: Why does the tortoise have a cracked shell in Nigerian folklore?
options: A god dropped him while creating the world
Birds took back their feathers and he fell from the sky after a greedy trick
He fought a lion and was stepped on during the battle
